source_text:
Ταπεινοφρονήσωμεν οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ἀλαζονείαν καὶ τῦφος καὶ ἀφροσύνην καὶ ὀργάς, καὶ ποιήσωμεν τὸ γεγραμμένον, λέγει γὰρ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον: Μὴ καυχάσθω ὁ σοφὸς ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ αὐτοῦ μηδὲ ὁ ἰσχυρὸς ἐν τῇ ἰσχύϊ αὐτοῦ μηδὲ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν τῷ πλούτῳ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ’ ἡ ὁ καυχώμενος ἐν κυρίῳ καυχάσθω, τοῦ ἐκζητεῖν αὐτὸν καὶ ποιεῖν κρίμα καὶ δικαιοσύνην: μάλιστα μεμνημένοι τῶν λόγων τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, οὓς ἐλάλησεν διδάσκων ἐπιείκειαν καὶ μακροθυμίαν.
οὕτως γὰρ εἶπεν: Ἐλεᾶτε, ἵνα ἐλεηθῆτε: ἀφίετε, ἵνα ἀφεθῇ ὑμῖν: ὡς ποιεῖτε, οὕτω ποιηθήσεται ὑμῖν: ὡς δίδοτε, οὕτως δοθήσεται ὑμῖν: ὡς κρίνετε, οὕτως κριθήσεσθε: ὡς χρηστεύεσθε, οὕτως χρηστευθήσεται ὑμῖν: ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε, ἐν αὐτῷ μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
ταύτῃ τῇ ἐντολῇ καὶ τοῖς παραγγέλμασιν τούτοις στηρίξωμεν ἑαυτοὺς εἰς τὸ πορεύεσθαι ὑπηκόους ὄντας τοῖς ἁγιοπρεπέσι λόγοις αὐτοῦ, ταπεινοφρονοῦντες: φησὶν γὰρ ὁ ἅγιος λόγος:
Ἐπὶ τίνα ἐπιβλέψω, ἀλλ’ ἢ ἐπὶ τὸν πραῢν καὶ ἡσύχιον καὶ τρέμοντά μου τὰ λόγια.
thought_title: Call to humility and the Lord's commands
orientation: The Roman church is addressing the Corinthians, urging them to abandon arrogance and obey the Lord's words on mercy and humility.
pass_a_gloss: Let us therefore be humble-minded, brothers, having put away all arrogance and conceit and folly and angers, and let us do what is written, for the Holy Spirit says: Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the strong man in his strength, nor the rich man in his wealth, but let him who boasts boast in the Lord, in seeking him and doing judgment and righteousness: especially remembering the words of the Lord Jesus, which he spoke teaching gentleness and patience. For thus he said: Show mercy, so that you may be shown mercy: forgive, so that it may be forgiven you: as you do, so it will be done to you: as you give, so it will be given to you: as you judge, so you will be judged: as you show kindness, so kindness will be shown to you: with what measure you measure, with that it will be measured to you. With this commandment and these instructions let us strengthen ourselves to walk being obedient to his holy words, being humble-minded: for the holy word says: Upon whom shall I look, except upon the gentle and quiet and the one who trembles at my words.

choices.why: τῦφος denotes puffed-up vanity or self-delusion; 'conceit' captures the inflated self-regard without the modern clinical sense of 'delusion'
ἀφροσύνη is lack of sense or foolishness; 'folly' preserves the moral and intellectual failure implied
ἐπιείκεια means reasonableness, fairness, or gentleness; 'gentleness' fits the context of the Lord's teaching on mercy and patience
χρηστεύομαι means to be kind or good; 'show kindness' preserves the active reciprocal force of the verb in the series of commands
ἁγιοπρεπής means befitting holiness or holy in character; 'holy' is concise and preserves the sense of words that are sacred and fitting for God
λόγια are oracles or sayings, especially divine utterances; 'words' is plain and preserves the sense of divine speech without the pagan connotation of 'oracles'

bible_refs.note: Μὴ καυχάσθω ὁ σοφὸς ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ αὐτοῦ μηδὲ ὁ ἰσχυρὸς ἐν τῇ ἰσχύϊ αὐτοῦ μηδὲ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν τῷ πλούτῳ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ’ ἢ ὁ καυχώμενος ἐν κυρίῳ καυχάσθω
Ἐπὶ τίνα ἐπιβλέψω, ἀλλ’ ἢ ἐπὶ τὸν πραῢν καὶ ἡσύχιον καὶ τρέμοντά μου τὰ λόγια

pass_b_english: So then, brothers and sisters, let us be humble-minded. Let us put away all arrogance, conceit, folly, and anger, and let us do what is written. For the Holy Spirit says: “Let not the wise boast in their wisdom, nor the strong in their strength, nor the rich in their riches; but let the one who boasts boast in the Lord, seeking him and doing justice and righteousness” (Jeremiah 9:23-24). Above all, let us remember the words of the Lord Jesus, which he spoke when he taught gentleness and patience.

For he said: “Show mercy, so that you may receive mercy. Forgive, so that you may be forgiven. As you do, so it will be done to you. As you give, so it will be given to you. As you judge, so you will be judged. As you show kindness, so kindness will be shown to you. With the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”

With this command and these instructions let us steady ourselves, so that we walk in obedience to his holy words, humble-minded. For the holy word says: “On whom will I look, but on the one who is gentle and quiet and trembles at my words?” (Isaiah 66:2).

polish.changed: Broke the opening sentence into two shorter sentences, clarified that the Holy Spirit is the speaker of the Jeremiah quotation, and kept the Lord Jesus as the clear subject of the second paragraph.

Clarified the flow between the Holy Spirit's quotation, the Lord Jesus's teaching, and the final scriptural quotation; made the speakers and pronouns explicit; smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and reference.

last_rejected.fix: So let us show humility, brothers and sisters
last_rejected.ruling: Ταπεινοφρονήσωμεν is a verb form; glossary entry for noun ταπεινοφροσύνη does not constrain verb rendering.

last_rejected.fix: in humility. For the holy word says
last_rejected.ruling: ταπεινοφρονοῦντες is a participle of ταπεινοφρονέω; glossary noun entry does not govern verb translation.

last_rejected.why: The quotation matches 1 Corinthians 1:31 / 2 Corinthians 10:17 (Paul citing Jeremiah), not Jeremiah directly in this form.
last_rejected.ruling: Source text closely follows Jeremiah 9:23-24 LXX wording; citation is defensible, not a major error.
